children: The projects span 14 districts and target 42,512 jobs across manufacturing, renewable energy, textiles and other sectors

Odisha has advanced 53 industrial projects involving investments of Rs 39,383 cr across 14 districts, with the potential to generate 42,512 jobs. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi inaugurated industrial facilities and laid foundation stones for new projects at Kalinganagar in Jajpur on 14 October 2026. The programme covered 46 industries across sectors including steel, metals, textiles, renewable energy, food processing, information technology, logistics and tourism, as the state seeks to translate investment commitments into manufacturing capacity and employment.

Steel and downstream manufacturing account for a significant share of the investment programme. Jindal Stainless and its group companies represent investments of Rs 14,039 cr across inaugurations and new project groundbreakings. Tata Steel’s projects include Rs 4,603 cr for downstream steel operations and Rs 3,329 cr for infrastructure.

Indian Metals and Ferro Alloys (IMFA) is undertaking projects worth Rs 1,900 cr, while Sree Metaliks has a proposed investment of Rs 1,575 cr. Other projects cover industrial gases, refractories, chemicals, plastics and logistics.

The programme also includes investments in renewable energy equipment, biofuels, electronics, apparel, shipbuilding, healthcare and tourism, reflecting efforts to diversify Odisha’s industrial base beyond its established metals and minerals sectors.
The projects span Angul, Bargarh, Balasore, Boudh, Cuttack, Dhenkanal, Jajpur, Jagatsinghpur, Kendujhar, Khordha, Mayurbhanj, Puri, Sambalpur and Sundargarh.

Alongside the 53 projects, the state announced 14 additional investment proposals comprising 12 memoranda of understanding and two investment intent forms. These represent a cumulative investment of Rs 4,805.66 cr and an estimated employment potential of 9,170.
The additional proposals are separate from the 53 projects covered by the inauguration and groundbreaking programme.

Majhi called for faster project execution, stronger local supply chains and more employment opportunities for young people. He emphasised the role of local enterprises, ancillary industries, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and entrepreneurs in extending the benefits of industrial investment across districts.

Industries Minister Sampad Chandra Swain highlighted the need to connect investment with workforce training, employment and vendor development. Pradeep Balasamanta, Minister for Cooperation, Handlooms, Textiles and Handicrafts, pointed to the employment potential of textile and apparel projects, particularly for women and young people.

The state government is coordinating project facilitation through the Industries Department, Industrial Promotion and Investment Corporation of Odisha (IPICOL), Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation (IDCO), district administrations and other departments. The objective is to address implementation bottlenecks and monitor progress towards commissioning.
During the programme, Majhi met industry representatives, participated in a roundtable with company leaders and visited IMFA and Jindal Stainless facilities in Kalinganagar.

Building on the Utkarsh Odisha, Make in Odisha Conclave 2025, the state is seeking to convert investment commitments into operating facilities and jobs. The initiative forms part of its Samruddha Odisha 2036 vision, aligned with the national goal of Viksit Bharat 2047.
